# ezghcloud_dns_record_set (Resource)

One record set (a name and type) of a zone. Record sets that another EZGH service manages, such as a domain authorization's validation records, can't be created, changed or deleted here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ezghcloud_dns_record_set" "www" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  zone_id    = ezghcloud_dns_zone.main.id
  name       = "www"
  type       = "A"
  ttl        = 300
  values     = ["192.0.2.1"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Lowercase name relative to the zone, or @ for the zone itself. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `project_id` (String) Project that holds the zone. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `type` (String) Record type, such as A, AAAA, CNAME or TXT. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `values` (Set of String) The record set's values.
- `zone_id` (String) Zone ID (zon_). Changing it replaces the record set.

### Optional

- `ttl` (Number) Time to live in seconds. Defaults to 300.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) zone_id/name/TYPE.
- `managed_by` (Attributes) The EZGH service that manages this record set, or null for a record set you manage. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--managed_by))

<a id="nestedatt--managed_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `managed_by`

Read-Only:

- `resource_name` (String) Resource name of the managing resource.
- `service` (String) Managing service namespace.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ezghcloud_dns_record_set.www zon_xxxxxxxxxxxx/www/A
```
